en: The Questions of King Milinda, Chapter on the Determination of Immaterial Phenomena: 15.
The Question on the Diversity of Consciousness.

“Venerable Nāgasena, are these things—‘consciousness’ (viññāṇa), ‘wisdom’ (paññā), and ‘the soul in the elements’ (bhūtasmiṃ jīvo)—different in meaning and different in phrasing, or are they one in meaning with only the phrasing being different?
“Consciousness, Great King, has the characteristic of cognizing; wisdom has the characteristic of understanding. As for the soul in the elements, it is not to be found.”
“If the soul is not apprehended, then who indeed sees a form with the eye,
hears a sound with the ear, smells an odor with the nose, tastes a flavor with the tongue, touches a tangible object with the body,
or cognizes a mental phenomenon with the mind?”

“If the soul sees forms with the eye … [and so on] … if it cognizes mental objects with the mind, then that soul, when the doors of the eyes are torn open, would see forms even more clearly facing outward through the great expanse of space; and when the ears are torn open, …”
“If the nose were torn out, the tongue were torn out, and the body were torn out, would one hear sound better,
smell odor, taste flavor, or touch the tangible through that great expanse of space?
“Therefore, Great King, in the elements no living being is found.
This was the fifteenth question, on the diversity of consciousness.
